evidence.ref: The warp.action/v1 contract (schema warp.action/v1, module .warp/action.py, 602 lines under the 1000 module_lines budget) and its structural validator validate_action FAIL CLOSED by name on every malformation class. An action declares the FAKE system it acts against (NG1), typed parameter specs (name, a type from string/integer/number/boolean/enum, a required flag, and a validation constraint), a risk class, a reversibility analysis (class/analysis/data_mutating), a rollback plan, a canary declaration (supported and, when supported, a shape), and a recorded review. validate_action refuses a wrong schema, a missing id/title/system, an out-of-vocabulary risk_class/reversibility class/parameter type/review status/review verdict, a malformed parameter spec (no name, an enum with no values, an inverted min/max range, an uncompilable pattern, a duplicate parameter name), a missing rollback, a missing canary declaration or a supported canary with no shape, a missing or malformed review block, and a file outside the parser subset. It reuses validate.parse_yamlish and validate.fail (no second parser, no import cycle) exactly as incident.py and decision.py do. The reference TRIO per D3 ships as clearly-illustrative fake-system examples (.warp/examples/action-rollback-deploy-example.yaml against fake-deploy-controller, action-restart-service-example.yaml against fake-service-controller, action-scale-pool-example.yaml against fake-pool-controller); each validates clean via python3 .warp/action.py .warp/examples/action-<name>-example.yaml.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1205 block: 'a well-formed warp.action/v1 record validates' (positive control) plus the refusal battery over a GOOD_ACTION fixture (wrong schema, missing id/system, out-of-vocab risk_class/reversibility class, missing analysis/data_mutating, malformed parser subset, missing rollback, missing canary, supported canary with no shape, parameter spec with no name / bad type / enum with no values / inverted range / uncompilable pattern / duplicate name, no review block, out-of-vocab review status, missing reviewer/reviewed_digest, reviewed-with-rejected-verdict contradiction), and 'the shipped action example <trio> validates' for each of the three.

A RUNBOOK ACTION CARRIES A HIGH RISK FLOOR AND NOTHING LOWERS A CLASS (C2). risk_floor(data) returns high for a reversible non-data-mutating action and critical when data_mutating is true or the reversibility class is irreversible; validate_action REFUSES an action whose declared risk_class ranks below its floor with the reason named, while a declaration at or above the floor is accepted (anything may raise a class, nothing may lower it, the same one-tier-ladder posture as the decision-record D5 mapping and the remedy two-key binding). The reference trio are all reversible, non-data-mutating, whitelist-floor high, and validate.

selftests: 'a data-mutating action declaring risk high is REFUSED (floor critical)'; 'an irreversible action declaring risk high is REFUSED (floor critical)'; 'an action declaring risk standard is REFUSED (below the high floor)'; positive controls 'a data-mutating action declaring critical validates' and 'a high-floor action declaring critical validates (a raise is allowed)'; and 'risk_floor is high for a reversible non-data-mutating action and critical for a data-mutating one'.

THE STORE REJECTS AN ACTION WITHOUT A RECORDED, DIGEST-CURRENT REVIEW. An action is code, reviewed through the normal WARP loop and promoted by a human; the review is recorded on the artifact and BOUND BY A DIGEST to the exact content it vetted (the WARP-0109 verdict-proof digest binding applied to a runbook action). action_digest is the action's own canonical digest over its reviewable substance excluding the review block; action_reviewed admits only a reviewed, approved, digest-current action; review_stale detects a reviewed action edited afterward and check_actions FAILS CLOSED on it (a vetted action cannot be silently edited). A PROPOSED action is a valid draft but is NOT admitted (it does not exist to the machine path until reviewed). The store performs no review itself (that is the loop's fresh-context vetting and human promotion); it enforces the recorded, digest-bound outcome, so unlike the responder and the adversarial decision reviewer it ships no delegated reasoner.

selftests: 'action_digest is deterministic and excludes the review block'; 'an action whose reviewed_digest matches its content is ADMITTED (action_reviewed True, review_stale False)'; 'the placeholder-digest action is NOT admitted'; THE STALE TOOTH 'editing a reviewed action (max 100 -> 200) makes the review STALE and it is NOT admitted'; 'a PROPOSED action is not stale but is NOT admitted (does not exist to the machine path)'; and the DRIFT GUARD 'the shipped action example <trio> is reviewed and digest-current' for each of the three.

ANYTHING NOT IN THE WHITELIST DOES NOT EXIST TO THE MACHINE PATH (O2/C4, NG2). An action reference is a whitelist KEY, never command text: resolve_action of an unknown reference returns None with NO free-form fallback, require_action REFUSES by name, and a shell-looking reference is unresolvable, not run; a present-but-unreviewed (proposed) action is likewise unresolvable. build_whitelist admits exactly the reviewed/approved/digest-current actions; check_actions is ADOPTION SAFE (no .warp/actions/ directory stands down, the effective whitelist empty) and FAILS CLOSED on a malformed action, a stale review, a duplicate id, and a required-but-absent action. validate_parameters refuses an unknown parameter, a missing required parameter, a wrong type, and a value outside the declared range/enum/pattern, each NAMING the parameter. warp.action/v1 BINDS INTO warp.remedy/v1 (W1): bind_remedy_action resolves a remedy's proposed_action reference against the whitelist (unknown/unreviewed refuses) and validates its parameters (out of range refuses by name), reusing the remedy dict W1 already parsed (no second parser); it RESOLVES and VALIDATES only and runs NOTHING (the executor W6 binds the resolved action to a proposal digest on its own credentials).

selftests over a temp .warp/actions/ tree holding the trio: 'check_actions passes'; 'build_whitelist admits EXACTLY the reviewed trio'; 'resolve_action resolves rollback_deploy and returns None for an unknown ref'; 'require_action REFUSES an unknown ref by name'; 'an action reference is NEVER interpreted as command text (a shell-looking ref is unresolvable)'; 'a non-string reference is unresolvable'; the W1 BINDING 'the shipped remedy example binds to the whitelist (rollback_deploy resolves and its parameters validate)', 'a remedy naming an action NOT in the whitelist is REFUSED', 'a remedy with an out-of-pattern parameter is REFUSED by name'; PARAMETER teeth (above max / below min / wrong type / unknown / missing required / out-of-enum / pattern mismatch each refuse by name, with valid positive controls); and adoption-safe + fail-closed directory postures (absent dir stands down; a proposed action passes the scan but is not admitted; a stale reviewed action fails closed; a malformed action fails closed; a duplicate id refused; a required-but-absent action fails closed).
